job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: During a sports period, Coach Meena gathered Rohan and Priya to discuss injury management. Rohan asked, 'If I twist my ankle but can still walk, it isn't broken, right?' Coach Meena shook her head, 'Not necessarily. A bone can be fractured even if it looks normal, so never assume it is fine just because you can bear weight.' Priya then asked about concussions, 'If a player hits their head but stays conscious, they are safe to keep playing, aren't they?' Coach Meena replied, 'Absolutely not. A concussion is a brain injury that does not require fainting to occur, and symptoms often develop hours later, not just immediately. You must stop play instantly if a head impact occurs.' Rohan then suggested using a hot pack for his swollen knee. Coach Meena corrected him, 'Never apply heat to a fresh injury, as it increases swelling. Instead, use the RICE method: Rest, Ice, Compression, and Elevation. When applying a compression bandage, ensure it is snug but not too tight, as restricting blood flow is dangerous. Finally, remember that RICE is just the first step; if pain persists or the injury seems severe, you must see a doctor immediately rather than waiting for it to heal on its own.'

items.evidence: A bone can be fractured even if it looks normal, so never assume it is fine just because you can bear weight.
items.q: Rohan twists his ankle but can still walk on it. What can he safely conclude?
options: It may still have a cracked bone
It cannot be broken since he walks
It is broken only if it looks bent
It will heal if he keeps walking
items.explain: A bone can be fractured even if it looks normal and can bear weight.

wrong.why: thinks bearing weight rules out a serious injury
thinks a broken bone always looks out of shape
thinks walking it off cures an injury

items.evidence: A concussion is a brain injury that does not require fainting to occur, and symptoms often develop hours later, not just immediately.
items.q: Asha bumps her head in a match, stays awake and feels fine. What should happen next?
options: She stops, as concussion can occur without fainting
She plays on, since she never fainted
She stops only if symptoms appear right away
She plays on through pain to look tough
items.explain: Concussion does not need fainting, and symptoms can appear hours later, so she must stop.

wrong.why: thinks playing through pain shows toughness

items.evidence: Coach Meena corrected him, 'Never apply heat to a fresh injury, as it increases swelling.
items.q: Rohan's knee swelled up just now. What would a hot pack do to it?
options: It would make the swelling worse
It would bring the swelling down
It would remove the need for rest
It would help only if he kept walking
items.explain: Heat on a fresh injury increases swelling, so ice should be used instead.

wrong.why: thinks one treatment replaces the RICE steps
thinks moving on an injury helps it

items.evidence: When applying a compression bandage, ensure it is snug but not too tight, as restricting blood flow is dangerous.
items.q: Priya wraps a compression bandage on a sprain as hard as she can. Is that right?
options: No, it may cut off the blood supply
Yes, since tighter always works better
Yes, if the leg is left hanging down
No, it works only with a hot pack
items.explain: The bandage should be snug, not too tight, because restricting blood flow is dangerous.

wrong.why: thinks a tighter bandage works better
thinks hanging the limb lets blood reach it
thinks heat helps a fresh injury

items.evidence: Finally, remember that RICE is just the first step; if pain persists or the injury seems severe, you must see a doctor immediately rather than waiting for it to heal on its own.'
items.q: After using RICE, Priya's ankle still hurts badly. What should she do now?
options: Get it checked by a doctor at once
Keep using RICE, since it treats everything
Stay in bed until it heals itself
Play through the pain to toughen up
items.explain: RICE is only the first step; if pain stays, see a doctor immediately.

wrong.why: thinks RICE alone treats any injury
thinks rest means days in bed and waiting
thinks playing through pain is right
